label: copy-phase input token h
explanation: Fires only when the input is h during the copy phase (the model fed back its own h output); every activation satisfies this (dev recall 1.0, precision 0.80). Never fires on h in the original phase or at the delimiter, nor on any other token. It is weak or absent when the h is the first copied token (recall_idx 1, i.e. sequences starting with h) and strongest at mid/late copy positions; a second h right after an h activates much more weakly than the first.

issues: Test scores match what was reported: P 0.805, R 0.99999, F1 0.892, mass recall 1.0. The only test-split activation the predicate misses is one at 0.07 (on a u).
The profile confirms zero activation in the original and delimiter phases and on every token other than h. All 73,538 dev activations are copy-phase h, with in_first always 0.

'Weak or absent at recall_idx 1' holds. Test precision for h at recall_idx==1 is 0.49, and that slice carries only 6.4% of activation mass while holding 11% of active steps. It accounts for about 8.3k of the 17.8k false positives.
'Repeated h is weaker' holds. h after h covers 2.5% of actives and 1.7% of mass, and top examples show the second h at 0.40 to 0.64 of the first.

'Strongest at middle and late positions' holds. Firing rate rises from about 0 at t=4 to about 0.03 at t>=10. The recall_idx>=2 & t<8 slice has precision 0.73 and L<=4 has 0.67, versus 0.90 for t>=10.

The leftover false positives are a smooth gradient rather than a separate class: early t, short L, and h occurring more than once in the original (in_count>=2 precision 0.80 vs 0.89). None of the refinements tried beat the base test F1: recall_idx>=2 gives 0.881, t>=8 gives 0.873, prev_tok!=h gives 0.883, and t>=7 gives 0.894, a negligible gain.
The label 'copy-phase input token h' matches the predicate exactly and does not overclaim.
